items.entity: volume fraction Vf of the cantilever-plate topology optimization
items.description: The Sec. 2.1 / Fig. 2 caption shows three runs, (b) Vf = 0.7, (c) 0.5 and (d) 0.3, and does not say which is the reference case. For the same cantilever, Sec. 4.1 gives Vf = 0.5 in the text (this matches V = 0.5·V̄ = 3900 cm³ = 0.5 × 7800 cm³ and Figs. 4b/18b), but the Fig. 12 caption gives Vf = 0.3.
readings: run all three, 0.7, 0.5 and 0.3, as the Fig. 2b–d sweep

items.entity: point load F = 100 kN on the free end
items.description: Secs. 2.1 and 4.1 give only the magnitude and the position ('as shown in Figure 2'); the direction appears only in Fig. 2a/12. The span/180 deflection check and the 'vertical downward deflection – positive' convention in Sec. 4.1 imply a transverse load. However, Tables 2–3 put the top chords (members 1, 3, 5) in compression and the bottom chords (12–14) in tension, which for a cantilever would mean an upward load (or a flipped image axis). Reversing a single vertical load does not change the compliance-optimal design; a non-vertical load would.
readings: vertical, upward (+y) – same TO optimum as downward
horizontal/axial or inclined (only if Fig. 2a showed it)

items.entity: finite-element grid resolution for the Fig. 2 runs
items.description: Neither Sec. 2.1 nor the Fig. 2 caption gives the discretization, even though Sec. 2.1 says 'different mesh sizes can vary these outputs'. Only Sec. 4.1 gives 150 × 52 × 1 elements (1 cm square elements) for the same cantilever.
readings: 150 × 52 elements of 1 cm × 1 cm (as in Sec. 4.1)

items.description: Sec. 1.3.1 says the domain is meshed with a 'structured grid and hexahedral linear elements' (Sec. 4.2 also uses 'linear hexahedral'), but Sec. 4.1 calls the cantilever mesh '150 × 52 × 1 linear quadrilateral elements'. For a single-layer hex model, the text also does not say how the point load is shared between the front and back nodes.
readings: 3D 8-node trilinear hexahedra, 150 × 52 × 1 (one 1 cm layer), point load split equally between the two through-thickness nodes

items.entity: 2D constitutive assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: For a 2D solver, the text never says whether the model is plane stress or plane strain. Secs. 1.3.1, 2.1 and 4.1 give only E = 2.1e5 N/mm², ν = 0.3 and a 1 cm thickness 'for size optimization'. Plane strain behaves like plane stress with ν' = ν/(1−ν) ≈ 0.43 (and a scaled E), so the optimum can shift slightly.

items.entity: out-of-plane thickness in the topology-optimization FE model
items.description: Secs. 2.1 and 4.1 give the 1 cm plate thickness only 'for size optimization'. The thickness used in the TO analysis is not stated. In a 2D plane-stress model it only scales stiffness and compliance.

The Fig. 2 caption (and Sec. 4.1) give R = 1.2 with no unit. Eq. (7) uses it as a distance between element centres, but the text never says whether it is in element widths or a physical length (cm). The two readings only coincide on the 1 cm (150 × 52) grid, so this ties in with the unknown mesh.
readings: 1.2 element widths (= 1.2 cm on the 150 × 52 grid; only the four edge neighbours get weight 0.2)
1.2 cm physical length, converted to element units if another mesh is used

items.entity: design-update scheme for the topology optimization
items.description: Sec. 1.3.1 derives the sensitivities for 'gradient-based optimization' but never names the TO update method or its parameters (move limit, damping, MMA asymptote settings). MMA and SQP are named only for the frame size/layout stage (Secs. 2.4, 4.1).
readings: Optimality Criteria with move limit 0.2 and damping exponent 0.5 (88-line style)
MMA (as used for the frame stage)

items.description: The Fig. 2 caption gives only 'Maximum iterations = 200'. No convergence tolerance is given for the TO stage; the tolerance of 1e-4 in Table 1 applies only to the frame size/layout optimization.
The starting design for the topology optimization is not stated in Sec. 1.3.1, Sec. 2.1 or Sec. 4.1.

items.entity: elements at the load point and along the fixed edge
items.description: No non-design (passive) elements are stated for the TO. However, Sec. 4.1 says 'fixed-end boundary pixels and force-applied pixels were tagged so no alteration is allowed during any stages of optimization' (see also 'loaded element pixel' in Figs. 4/18). It is unclear whether this means those elements were held solid during TO or were only tags for skeletonization and the frame model.
readings: loaded element(s) at the load point held solid (ρ = 1)
loaded element(s) plus the column of elements along the fixed edge held solid
